## Design

### 2026-10-07 – Today, I installs Kicad and all the necessary extra footprints and symbols. Then, I followed the tutorial for the Starbie's schematics (making an effort to understand why I was doing what I was doing

**4h**

Today, I installs Kicad and all the necessary extra footprints and symbols. Then, I followed the tutorial for the Starbie's schematics (making an effort to understand why I was doing what I was doing at the same time). Finally, after some trouble, I have succeeded in arranging the PCB in the PCB editor, and wired it.

Learning the ropes of Kicad was a longer process than I expected, taking around 1.5 hours just to construct the segments in the schematic, but beyond that, I have made fast progress in my knowledge of the application.

The only difficulty to add is that my wiring looks nothing like the tutorial (it is significantly more messy). I will attempt to fix this when I next work on the project. Along with that, I also need to test the PCB, then I can move on to coding!

### 2026-10-08 – After a little while spent downloading and figuring out Arduino (another new program I haven't used before), I managed to copy the tutorials code over, and make some changes. I added the "sparkle" pro

**6h**

After a little while spent downloading and figuring out Arduino (another new program I haven't used before), I managed to copy the tutorials code over, and make some changes. I added the "sparkle" program and unfortunately was limited by not having an ESP32 to upload onto yet (if you are reading this, please let me know if I need one this week or if I was getting ahead of myself).

I then spent the rest of my time attempting (to little but non-negligible success), rewiring my PCB design to minimise the amount of unnecessary wires and try and simplify it a bit.
